description:
pkix-ct/src/lib.rs:94-96 — verify_scts always returns Err(Error::NoTrustedSct):
  `pub fn verify_scts(_cert: &Certificate, _logs: &CtLogList) -> Result<()> { Err(Error::NoTrustedSct) }`

The crate-level doc comment says 'Not yet implemented' and the README shows pkix-ct as 'planned'. However:

1. The function signature is public and exported — callers can call it and will always get an error. There is no #[deprecated] or compile-time indication it is a stub.
2. A caller who calls verify_scts trusting it does something will get a false error on all certs.

Suggested fix: Add #[deprecated = "pkix-ct is not yet implemented"] to the verify_scts function, or make it return a specific error variant (Error::NotImplemented) and document that variant as the stub indicator. The README already says 'planned' so this is just an in-code disambiguation.

P3 — misleading public API.
title: pkix-ct verify_scts always returns NoTrustedSct — unimplemented stub not documented in README
